role.altitude: The robotics engineer keeps defining interfaces, wiring cells, running experiments, judging performance and deciding research directions; retyping I/O lists into controllers, timing cycles with a stopwatch, comparing program versions by hand and typing maintenance notes shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An engineer whose cell documentation stays current by itself.

tasks.short: Define interfaces, mount and wire peripherals, configure communication and I/O mapping, test the integrated cell, and record settings to integrate robotics with peripherals such as welders and controllers.

steps.what: Engineer defines interfaces and signals between the robot and peripherals
Engineer mounts and wires welders, controllers and other peripherals
Engineer configures communication and I/O mapping in the robot controller
Engineer tests the integrated cell
Engineer records the integration settings

tasks.design: The I/O mapping is imported into the robot controller from the cell's device list, instead of being typed signal by signal. Defining interfaces, mounting, wiring and testing stay hands-on.
tasks.previous_blocker: Signals were typed into the controller from a printed list.
tasks.human_edge: Finding why a welder misses its trigger one time in a hundred.

reach.learn: Whether I/O errors at start-up fall.

evidence.claim: An industrial assistant writes control code and HMI screens in an engineering platform.

assumptions: Boundary: integrating peripherals; device lists and timing charts (task 16513) and documenting changes (task 16514) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s3: device lists made in task 16513 in an importable format, for about 60% of cells; s3 is priced at that share.
s5 is part of documenting application changes, which task 16514 covers; its saving is counted there.
Defining, wiring and testing keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of controllers that import I/O lists.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older controllers; high: modern controllers with import.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Define criteria and test cases, run test cycles, collect performance data, evaluate robotic systems or prototypes against the criteria, and write the evaluation.

steps.what: Engineer defines evaluation criteria and test cases
Engineer runs test cycles on the robot
Engineer collects performance data: cycle time, accuracy and errors
Engineer evaluates the robotic systems or prototypes against the criteria
Engineer writes the evaluation report

tasks.design: The robot controller logs cycle times, positions and error codes, and an export feeds a dashboard per test case, instead of the engineer timing cycles and noting errors by hand. The report template places the dashboard tables. Defining criteria, running tests and evaluating stay with the engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cycle times and errors were noted by hand.
tasks.still_hard: Quality judgements such as weld appearance.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a motion that will wear a joint early.

reach.learn: Whether acceptance rests on more cycles.

evidence.claim: Test data suit dashboards and statistics.

assumptions: Boundary: evaluating robotic systems; building, configuring and testing robots (task 21057) is a sibling task.
s2 is part of testing robotic applications, which sibling task 21057 covers; its saving is counted there.
Input contract for s3: about 70% of controllers export logs; s3 is priced at that share.
Defining and evaluating keep their full time.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older controllers; high: controllers with full logging.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Define questions, review prior work, simulate mechanisms, build and run experiments, and analyse findings to research the feasibility, design, operation or performance of robotic mechanisms, components or systems.

steps.what: Engineer defines the research questions on feasibility or performance
Engineer reviews prior work and literature

loop.input: The research questions and a literature database.
loop.output: A ranked list of papers with short summaries, each linked to its source.
loop.check: The engineer opens every cited paper before use; summaries are never quoted.
loop.stop: The engineer searches by hand when known key papers are missing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Robotics work spreads over many venues and terms.

steps.what: Engineer simulates the robotic mechanisms
Engineer builds and runs experiments
Engineer analyses the findings

tasks.design: A literature search returns ranked papers with linked summaries, and the engineer opens every source before use. Simulation runs for parameter variations are scripted. Defining questions, experiments and analysis stay with the engineer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Literature was searched by hand and simulations set up one by one.
tasks.enabler_now: Literature search with citations and scripted simulation.
tasks.still_hard: Mechanisms with contact and friction the simulator handles poorly.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which idea is worth building.

reach.learn: Whether reviews of prior work are more complete.

evidence.claim: A simulation tool predicts new designs from past simulations; the vendor claims 10 to 100 times shorter cycles.
In a benchmark, the best strategy made executable simulation calls 88% of the time; executable is not correct.

assumptions: Boundary: researching robotic mechanisms; research to create new systems (task 16523) is a sibling task.
Defining, experimenting and analysing keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of research time spent on literature.
research_questions: Does the literature review miss fewer key papers?

already_counted.description: Engineer opens and checks every cited paper.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: experiment-heavy work; high: literature and simulation-heavy work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Record program changes and reasons, update the application description and instructions, update I/O and parameter lists, log maintenance, and release the documents to document robotic application development, maintenance or changes.

steps.what: Engineer records program changes and their reasons
Engineer updates the robotic application description and operating instructions

loop.input: The program difference between versions and the engineer's change notes.
loop.output: Draft updates to the affected sections of the description and instructions.
loop.check: Every described change must appear in the program difference; any extra stops the draft; the engineer edits.
loop.stop: The engineer updates the sections by hand after two failed checks.
loop.why_not_simpler: Instructions describe behaviour, not code lines.

steps.what: Engineer updates I/O lists and parameter sheets
Engineer logs maintenance done and parts replaced
Engineer files the documents and mails them to the team

tasks.design: Robot programs are kept under version control, so the difference between versions is shown automatically and the engineer only writes the reason, instead of comparing versions and listing changes by hand. A drafting step updates the affected sections of the description and instructions from that difference, and the engineer edits. I/O lists and parameter sheets are exported from the controller project. Maintenance is logged on a tablet form linked to the robot, instead of paper notes typed up later. Release in document control notifies the team, instead of mailed attachments.
tasks.previous_blocker: Changes were found by comparing programs and documents updated by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Version control for robot programs and controller exports.
tasks.still_hard: Changes made on the teach pendant without saving a version.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining why a change was made, for whoever touches it next.

reach.learn: Whether documentation matches the running program.

evidence.claim: Documents are drafted from records by a bounded loop; every fact traces to a record and the engineer signs.

assumptions: Boundary: documenting development, maintenance and changes; backing up robot programs (task 16516) is a sibling task.
Version control also keeps program copies; that saving belongs to task 16516 and is not counted here.
s4 saves the second entry of paper maintenance notes; s5 saves the mail transport of documents.
Input contract for s3: about 70% of controllers export I/O and parameters; s3 is priced at that share.
unknowns: Number of program changes per month.
research_questions: Do documents match running programs more often?

incremental.description: Engineer commits pendant changes to version control.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few changes and older controllers; high: frequent changes on modern controllers.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
